description: 40 canonical screen records with AI hooks and acceptance scenarios. Proposed design, not implemented features.

screens.title: Home / Project Hub
screens.placement: Home icon; launcher, not persistent editing tab
screens.purpose: The entry point for opening, creating, recovering and learning about projects; must never imply active engine features that do not exist.
screens.surface: Project list/card grid with thumbnails, recent files, version/compatibility indicators and a compact new/open/import action strip. No giant banner once a project is open.
screens.panels: Recent projects, templates, recovery sessions, engine/runtime selection, update notices, tutorials and verified plugin compatibility.
screens.actions: Create, open, clone, restore, rename, reveal in file manager; search and sort; confirm conversion when a project schema is older.
screens.data: ProjectManifest, recent-project cache, template catalogue, recovery snapshots and engine capability manifest.
screens.connections: Opens P40 wizard, P38 settings and P24 assets; launch enters P02 World or saved last workspace.
screens.backend: ProjectManager, filesystem, version migration detector, template installer, recents index, crash recovery.
screens.acceptance: A valid new project opens and can be reloaded; a corrupt or unsupported project gives actionable errors without changing files.
screens.ai: Search templates and explain missing SDK/plugin requirements; suggest recovery options without modifying projects.
screens.verificationScenario: Open/recover a project on an unfamiliar machine.

screens.title: World Editor
screens.placement: Primary World workspace
screens.purpose: Assemble gameplay worlds with a scene hierarchy and real renderer, while preserving direct access to terrain, lighting, physics and scripting.
screens.surface: Large perspective/orthographic Vulkan viewport with selection, translate/rotate/scale gizmos, snapping, camera controls, debug overlays and Play/Simulate.
screens.panels: Scene Outliner; content dock; details/Inspector; World Settings; contextual Terrain, Foliage, Lighting, Layers and Navigation submodes.
screens.actions: Create/delete/duplicate/reparent entities; multi-select; group, hide, lock, align, spawn prefab, drag asset into level; save/reopen.
screens.data: SceneDocument, entity IDs, Transform, MeshRenderer, Camera, Light and world/streaming settings.
screens.connections: Meshes from P03/P04; materials P05/P06; lights P29; terrain P30; physics P19; AI/nav P35; playtest P21.
screens.backend: ECS+SceneGraph, Vulkan renderer, selection picking, spatial index, command bus, serialization, undo and asset registry.
screens.acceptance: Moving an entity updates viewport, Outliner, Inspector and serialized scene; reopening preserves hierarchy, transformations and assets.
screens.ai: Plan terrain/prop placement; preview entity transforms, asset dependencies, world cells and validation checks.
screens.verificationScenario: Modify one visible entity and persist it.

screens.title: 3D Modeling Studio
screens.placement: Create > Modeling; mesh asset editor
screens.purpose: Create editable polygonal props and game-ready mesh assets without leaving the editor, eventually matching professional topology workflows.
screens.surface: Main mesh-edit viewport with vertex/edge/face selections, shaded/wireframe overlays, normals, transform handles and LOD statistics.
screens.panels: Object tree, modifier stack, mesh data inspector, UV tab, topology analysis, material slots and modeling history.
screens.actions: Primitives, extrude, inset, bevel, loop cut, bridge, merge, split, mirror, arrays, booleans, triangulate, UV unwrap and apply modifier.
screens.data: Editable MeshAsset, mesh topology ID mapping, modifiers/history, material assignments, UV sets, LOD metadata.
screens.connections: Shares editable mesh with P04 Sculpt, P05 Texture, P06 Material, P07 Character, P19 Physics and World P02.
screens.backend: Geometry kernels, half-edge or equivalent topology representation, CPU/GPU mesh editing, spatial queries, import/export.
screens.acceptance: A user edits geometry, performs undo/redo, saves and sees updated mesh in an existing scene with references intact.
screens.ai: Propose editable topology/LOD variants; validate manifoldness, UVs and mesh scale before material/rig export.
screens.verificationScenario: Edit a vertex/edge/face and update asset references.

screens.title: Sculpting Studio
screens.placement: Create > Sculpt; mesh asset mode
screens.purpose: Perform high-resolution non-destructive surface authoring for characters, environments and hero assets.
screens.surface: Dominant clay/material preview with brush cursor, symmetry visualization, masks, detail levels and interactive navigation.
screens.panels: Brush shelf, multiresolution/remesh controls, sculpt object tree, layer stack, alpha library, topology/polygon count, masks.
screens.actions: Draw, clay, crease, smooth, grab, inflate, flatten, scrape, symmetry, alpha stamps, mask, voxel remesh, dynamic topology and bake.
screens.data: SculptAsset, stroke journal or layers, mesh levels, masks, brush settings and high-poly/low-poly relationships.
screens.connections: Model P03 provides base mesh; Texture P05 receives baked details; Character P07 receives shapes; Asset Hub P24 tracks results.
screens.backend: Spatial brush acceleration, subdivision/remeshing, mesh multiresolution, safe GPU preview and memory budgeting.
screens.acceptance: Strokes are reproducible and undoable; topology operations preserve meaningful asset links or explicitly report required rebakes.
screens.ai: Suggest non-destructive brushes, masks, remesh/retopo tasks and preserve editable layers.
screens.verificationScenario: Sculpt one mesh at multiple subdivision levels.

screens.title: Texture Studio
screens.placement: Create > Texture; material texture-set mode
screens.purpose: Paint, layer, bake and export physically based texture maps while viewing the final material on the target asset.
screens.surface: Dual 3D model preview and 2D UV/texture canvas with selectable channel (base color, roughness, metalness, normal, AO, height, emissive).
screens.panels: Texture set list, brush/stencil shelf, paint layers, masks, smart materials, baking settings, channel thumbnails, export presets.
screens.actions: Paint, projection, fill, erase, mask, clone, smart wear/dirt, bake normal/AO/curvature, adjust channel bit depth and reimport.
screens.data: TextureSet, layer stack, source images, masks, UV relationships, color-space metadata, bake dependencies.
screens.connections: UVs from P03; high-poly normals from P04; P06 material graph consumes texture outputs; World P02 updates in situ.
screens.backend: Brush engine, GPU paint surfaces, image codecs, bake pipeline, color management, tile/UDIM design, undo transactions.
screens.acceptance: A changed paint layer updates a linked material and reopens without destructive flattening; game export uses baked textures.
screens.ai: Generate licensed PBR map candidates, seam-aware paint tasks and channel/color-space validation.
screens.verificationScenario: Paint a PBR mask and inspect multiple maps.

screens.title: Material Studio
screens.placement: Create > Materials; opens by material asset
screens.purpose: Build reusable surface appearances using PBR parameters and a validated graph rather than hard-coded shader values.
screens.surface: Realtime material preview on sphere/mesh/scene with environment lighting plus an optional central node graph editor.
screens.panels: Material library, node palette, graph canvas, texture channels, static/dynamic parameters, blend modes, instances and compile errors.
screens.actions: Create material, change parameters, wire nodes, create instance, preview shader permutations, inspect compilation and reset values.
screens.data: MaterialGraph, MaterialInstance, TextureRef, ShaderVariant, render-state and compile metadata.
screens.connections: P05 produces maps; P28 owns advanced shader code/graph; P29 controls preview lighting; P02 and P07 use instances.
screens.backend: Material expression graph, shader compiler, parameter binding, variant caching, render-state validation and hot reload.
screens.acceptance: Changing a material instance changes referenced objects without altering its parent; shader errors leave the last valid material visible.
screens.ai: Generate material parameter variants and shader graph proposals; run compile and visual comparisons.
screens.verificationScenario: Create a reusable material instance.

screens.title: Character Studio
screens.placement: Character workspace; character asset editor
screens.purpose: Assemble game-ready characters from geometry, shape controls, materials, garments and equipment in a traceable workflow.
screens.surface: Turntable 3D character preview with front/side/back views and optional wireframe, hair, skin, UV and rig diagnostic panes.
screens.panels: Character/preset library, body and facial morphs, wardrobe/equipment slots, expression thumbnails, hair/groom, LOD and validation.
screens.actions: Choose base archetype, edit morphs, attach armor, assign materials, inspect LOD, generate a character prefab and send to rigging.
screens.data: CharacterAsset, body/face morphs, slot attachment refs, materials, meshes, skeleton link and game-ready validation report.
screens.connections: Models P03, sculpt P04 and texture P05 feed character; rig P08 and animation P09 consume; physics P19 cloth later.
screens.backend: Character assembly and dependency graph, morph evaluation, skinning binding, LOD generation/validation, prefab system.
screens.acceptance: A character created from interchangeable assets retains valid rig/material references and can be placed as a prefab in P02.
screens.ai: Draft character variants, outfits and LODs using project style constraints and licensing provenance.
screens.verificationScenario: Create a character variant linked to a rig.

screens.title: Rigging Studio
screens.placement: Character > Rig; specialized rig asset editor
screens.purpose: Create, skin and inspect skeletal rigs for animation, procedural control and runtime posing.
screens.surface: Character in T/A pose with color-coded skeleton bones, IK/FK manipulators, gizmos and weight-paint diagnostic overlay.
screens.panels: Bone hierarchy, controls/constraints list, IK setup, weight brush settings, influence heatmaps, pose library and retarget mapping.
screens.actions: Add/reparent/orient/mirror bones, bind skin, paint/normalize weights, configure control rig and IK, validate hierarchy and retarget.
screens.data: SkeletonAsset, BindPose, SkinWeights, ControlRig, Constraints, RetargetProfile and bone GUID mapping.
screens.connections: P07 sources the character; P09 consumes rig for clips; P19 ragdoll maps physics bodies to bones; P12 cinematics pose rig.
screens.backend: Skeletal skinning, constraint graph, IK solvers, vertex influences, bone mapping and non-destructive import.
screens.acceptance: A skinned character animates without unexplained deformation; bone changes invalidate dependent clips with clear migration guidance.
screens.ai: Suggest bone hierarchy/weights/IK; detect deformation, rig mismatch and animation-retarget impact.
screens.verificationScenario: Retarget a skeleton and verify deformation.

screens.title: Animation Studio
screens.placement: Animation workspace; clip/state-machine asset tabs
screens.purpose: Author clips and movement logic for skeletal, prop, camera and event animation across gameplay and cinematics.
screens.surface: Dominant character/scene preview above resizable timeline, dope sheet and curve editor; optional animation state graph.
screens.panels: Animation asset tree, clip/take list, layers, IK controls, retargeting, animation notifies, compression, root-motion inspector.
screens.actions: Keyframe, scrub, adjust tangents, layer, blend, retarget, attach event, set transitions, preview controller and export clips.
screens.data: AnimationClip, keyframe tracks, curve tangents, layer stack, state machine, bone references, notifies and compression settings.
screens.connections: Consumes P08 rigs; drives P02 actors and P21 playtest; triggers P11 audio and P10 VFX; P12 sequences reuse same clips.
screens.backend: Interpolation and blend trees, skeleton evaluation, retargeter, event dispatcher, deterministic preview, optimized runtime playback.
screens.acceptance: Selected clip updates its bound preview rig; notifies fire at the same logical frames in playtest and packaged runtime.
screens.ai: Propose keyframes/retargeted actions/blend transitions; test root motion and foot planting.
screens.verificationScenario: Blend two animations and play in the world.

screens.title: VFX Studio / Particle Graph
screens.placement: VFX workspace; Niagara-like original graph
screens.purpose: Author high-impact real-time particles and effects using WorldForge-owned node graphs and a predictable GPU/CPU preview.
screens.surface: Effect preview viewport with particles, bounds and debug counters next to graph, curves and multi-emitter timeline.
screens.panels: Emitter library, node graph, spawn/render modules, system inspector, material slots, event tracks, variation thumbnails, performance.
screens.actions: Build emitter, connect modules, author spawn/lifetime/forces/color curves, collision, trails, events, preview, profile and set LOD.
screens.data: VFXGraph, Emitter, ParticleModule, ResourceBinding, MaterialRef, GPU program and event descriptors.
screens.connections: P06 shaders/materials, P09 notifies, P12 cinematics, P19 physics and P02 scene placement all consume VFX assets.
screens.backend: Typed graph compiler, GPU simulation buffers, resource binding, deterministic seed management, effect bounds/scalability.
screens.acceptance: An effect can be edited and reloaded while in a scene; invalid graph connections are rejected with explanatory errors.
screens.ai: Plan effects graphs, emitter budgets and consistent variants; profile GPU/CPU and particle lifetime.
screens.verificationScenario: Create an effect from a reusable graph.

screens.title: Audio Studio
screens.placement: Audio workspace; audio asset/mix editor
screens.purpose: Arrange and mix sound effects, dialogue, ambience and adaptive music for a game, retaining a connection to in-world emitters.
screens.surface: Multitrack waveform/timeline and mixer, with an embedded video or 3D viewport preview for synchronized sound design.
screens.panels: Asset library, tracks, buses, FX rack, fades, markers, automation, event graph, meters, ducking and loudness/peak analysis.
screens.actions: Import, trim, fade, loop, mix, route, normalize, create event cues, add bus effects, preview and prepare streamed/compressed output.
screens.data: AudioAsset, Clip, Track, MixBus, AutomationCurve, EventCue, ImportMetadata and spatial emitter reference.
screens.connections: P33 spatial tab handles 3D positioning; P12 sequences reference cues; P09 notifies trigger SFX; P21 tests runtime sound.
screens.backend: miniaudio backend initially, sample-accurate graph/mixer later, decoding and resampling, streaming and real-time-safe audio threads.
screens.acceptance: Audio cue playback works in editor and runtime; playback is synchronized and no UI-thread operation blocks the real-time audio callback.
screens.ai: Find sound assets, propose mix/effect chains and check clipping/loudness/rights.
screens.verificationScenario: Place and mix multiple sound sources.

screens.title: Cinematic Studio
screens.placement: Cinematic workspace; Sequencer editor
screens.purpose: Create cameras, shots, cutscenes, dialogue and presentation sequences using the actual game scene and assets.
screens.surface: Camera viewport with safe frames and cinematic framing plus multi-camera preview, shot list and large dockable sequencer.
screens.panels: Sequence browser, camera/lens inspector, camera cuts, actor/light/audio/VFX tracks, color controls, film/render queue.
screens.actions: Create shot, place camera, keyframe lens/transform, edit cuts, sync dialogue, apply color look, test cutscene and render preview.
screens.data: CinematicSequence, Shot, CameraRig, Track, AssetRefs, RenderQueueJob, ColorLook settings.
screens.connections: Shares P02 scenes, P07 characters, P09 animation, P10 VFX and P11 audio; output can feed P27 trailer assets.
screens.backend: Timeline sequencer, frame-accurate event scheduler, camera model, offline frame capture/encoder pipeline later.
screens.acceptance: Sequence playback reproduces camera cuts and animation/audio events; saving does not create disconnected copies of actors.
screens.ai: Suggest shot list, camera positions, continuity, cuts and timing; leave tracks editable.
screens.verificationScenario: Create a shot sequence and render a preview.

screens.title: Programming Studio (C++)
screens.placement: Gameplay > Code; source-file tabs
screens.purpose: Provide a real C++ programming and debugging environment tightly linked to engine objects, without forcing visual scripting.
screens.surface: Tabbed code editor with syntax diagnostics, quick navigation, breakpoints and source map, complemented by logs and debugger docks.
screens.panels: Project tree, symbol outline, problems, build output, call stack, watches, variables, search, revision info and documentation.
screens.actions: Create/open source, navigate definitions, compile, run player, debug breakpoints, inspect variables and open owning scene/entity.
screens.data: C++ source files, compile_commands.json, module manifest, build graph, diagnostics, debugger symbol references.
screens.connections: Creates gameplay components used by P02 World and P21 Playtest; P14 Visual Scripting later invokes exposed APIs; P18 builds.
screens.backend: CMake compiler integration, LSP/clangd, debugger adapter, safe build process, module reload strategy and reflection metadata.
screens.acceptance: Code compiles into a loadable game module with diagnostics linked to lines; debugger pauses game execution and inspects state.
screens.ai: Read code symbols via RAG, propose C++ patches with diff review, compilation and tests.
screens.verificationScenario: Edit/compile a C++ component and review diagnostics.

screens.title: Visual Scripting (Blueprint-style)
screens.placement: Gameplay > Graph; graph asset editor
screens.purpose: Let creators build typed gameplay logic using original visual graph tooling without relying on Unreal technology or copying its APIs.
screens.surface: Pan/zoom node canvas with typed pins, wires, comments, reroutes and breakpoint highlights, plus runtime preview.
screens.panels: Node palette, asset tree, variables/functions/events, component list, Inspector, compiler results, graph debugger and preview.
screens.actions: Add events/functions, wire pins, define variables, compile graph, step through execution, watch values and refactor subgraphs.
screens.data: GameplayGraph, NodeID, PinID, FunctionSignature, VariableMetadata, Bytecode/compiled plan, debug mapping.
screens.connections: Can attach graphs to P02 entities; graph nodes expose native C++ components from P13; supports P21 and P22 debugging/tests.
screens.backend: Typed graph schema, compiler/interpreter, reflection registry, runtime graph scheduler, cycle/type validation and trace support.
screens.acceptance: A user can create input -> movement behavior, inspect validation errors and replay behavior in a standalone player.
screens.ai: Generate typed visual graphs; verify pin types, cycle restrictions, determinism and runtime semantics.
screens.verificationScenario: Construct/validate a visual script behavior.

screens.title: NPC AI / Behavior Tools
screens.placement: Gameplay > NPC AI; behavior tree and nav tabs
screens.purpose: Author in-game agent behavior rather than generic text generation: perception, states, navigation, decisions and debugging.
screens.surface: AI simulation viewport with perception cones, paths and agent labels plus behavior-tree or state-machine graph.
screens.panels: NPC library, behavior tree, blackboard, EQS/query visualizer, perception settings, navmesh and agent state/events.
screens.actions: Create behavior, define priorities, connect blackboard keys, configure sight/hearing, debug transitions and validate nav paths.
screens.data: AIController, BehaviorTree, Blackboard, PerceptionConfig, NavQuery, AgentRuntimeTelemetry.
screens.connections: Depends on P35 navigation, P02 world and P13 gameplay; debug in P21; automate scenarios through P22 testing.
screens.backend: Behavior tree interpreter, perception queries, pathfinding, navmesh runtime, agent scheduler and state-recording debugger.
screens.acceptance: Given a simple patrol scenario, the same NPC follows routes, reacts to a stimulus and recovers to patrol reproducibly.
screens.ai: Generate constrained NPC state machine/behavior tree and dialogue rules; test perceptual responses.
screens.verificationScenario: Make guard NPC patrol, notice and pursue.

screens.title: Multiplayer Studio
screens.placement: Gameplay > Multiplayer; dedicated sub-editor
screens.purpose: Manage sessions, replication, client/server simulation, networking budgets and multiplayer validation.
screens.surface: Multi-client gameplay preview plus replication graph and latency/bandwidth charts with independent server/client consoles.
screens.panels: Session configs, replication rules, client table, dedicated server profiles, join/match flow, prediction diagnostics, network emulation.
screens.actions: Host/join locally, launch N clients, inspect replicated fields, induce latency/loss, record desync and package server build.
screens.data: SessionConfig, NetworkProfile, ReplicationPolicy, NetworkEntityID, TransportSettings, CapturedTrace.
screens.connections: P13 components expose serializable state; P21 launches sessions; P22 runs tests; P23 profiles network; P18 builds headless server.
screens.backend: Transport abstraction, authoritative simulation, state serialization, interpolation/prediction, interest management, security.
screens.acceptance: Two players interact with the same object consistently under simulated latency; server authority rejects invalid client edits.
screens.ai: Propose replicated properties and server validation checks; generate latency/packet-loss test cases.
screens.verificationScenario: Simulate latency and inspect replication.

screens.title: UI Testing Mode
screens.placement: Testing > UI; launched from UI Designer
screens.purpose: Validate game user interfaces across resolutions, inputs, localization and accessibility, without duplicating the UI authoring workspace.
screens.surface: Game UI test viewport with bounds, focus order and visual-diff overlays alongside test and recorder docks.
screens.panels: Widget hierarchy, smoke tests, input recorder, assertion list, baseline/current image comparison, keyboard/gamepad navigation.
screens.actions: Record action sequence, simulate input, assert text/focus/state, compare screenshots, export failure evidence and rerun tests.
screens.data: UITestCase, InputTrace, ExpectedWidgetState, ScreenshotBaseline, AccessibilityResults.
screens.connections: UI layouts from P20; P21 runtime events; P22 QA suite; P27 release validation gate.
screens.backend: Headless UI runner, test hooks, screenshot comparator, accessibility inspector, deterministic UI state serializer.
screens.acceptance: A Continue button test passes by keyboard and mouse, fails with meaningful evidence when the button is missing or disabled.
screens.ai: Generate keyboard/responsive/accessibility test cases and evidence-based visual-diff reports.
screens.verificationScenario: Verify a HUD in 1080p and 4K with accessibility.

screens.title: Build System
screens.placement: Build workspace or Build menu
screens.purpose: Compile code and cook project resources reproducibly into a launchable game artifact with inspectable logs and profiles.
screens.surface: Build configuration editor, target selector, asset-cooking status, build queue, console log, artifacts table and size budget charts.
screens.panels: Platform profiles, optimization levels, output directories, incremental/full build, release symbols, asset-cook per-type progress.
screens.actions: Validate, queue/cancel/retry build, inspect failed step, open artifact, compare sizes, run player and generate signed manifests later.
screens.data: BuildProfile, CookGraph, BuildJob, ToolchainManifest, Artifact, BuildReport, ContentHashCache.
screens.connections: Consumes all project assets; reports failures to P22 QA and P39 Console; successful artifacts transfer to P27 Publishing.
screens.backend: Headless WorldForgeBuild executable, dependency graph, content hashing/cook cache, native compiler, packager and target profiles.
screens.acceptance: From a clean checkout, a specified Windows project builds deterministically enough to run and produces a machine-readable report.
screens.ai: Explain build errors, propose settings changes and run authorized, reproducible cook/package tests.
screens.verificationScenario: Create reproducible Windows build artifacts.

screens.title: Physics Studio
screens.placement: Effects/Simulation > Physics; world context or physics asset
screens.purpose: Create rigid-body and collision behavior, then extend toward vehicles, cloth, ragdolls and destruction.
screens.surface: Simulation viewport with collision shapes, contact points, bounds, forces, selectable bodies and fixed-step playback controls.
screens.panels: Physics asset tree, body/shape inspector, constraints graph, materials, debug overlays, live profiler and simulation timeline.
screens.actions: Add body/collider, assign mass/friction/restitution, link joints, simulate/pause/step/reset, inspect contacts and save presets.
screens.data: PhysicsBody, ColliderShape, Joint, PhysicsMaterial, WorldPhysicsSettings and collision-layer matrix.
screens.connections: Mesh colliders from P03, ragdolls P08, world entities P02, destruction/VFX P10/P34 and runtime P21.
screens.backend: Jolt adapter, shape cooking, fixed-step simulation, debug draw, collision filtering and serialization.
screens.acceptance: A box reliably falls onto a floor in Editor preview and WorldForgePlayer; collision and transform changes remain synchronized.
screens.ai: Suggest collider shapes/joints/mass; run bounded simulation checks and report stability.
screens.verificationScenario: Drop a crate on a destructible prop safely.

screens.title: UI Designer
screens.placement: UI workspace; UI layout asset
screens.purpose: Design menus, HUDs and interactive game interfaces visually with keyboard/gamepad/accessibility support.
screens.surface: WYSIWYG screen canvas with guides, anchors, breakpoints and responsive-device preview; selected widget handles visible.
screens.panels: Widget tree, palette, properties, themes/style guide, state preview, bindings, animation timeline, localization and a11y checks.
screens.actions: Drag controls, set anchors, theme states, bind gameplay data, design focus navigation, preview at aspect ratios and save layouts.
screens.data: UILayout, WidgetTree, StyleSheet, AnimationTrack, DataBinding, LocalizationKey and FocusNavigationGraph.
screens.connections: P17 tests UI, P21 displays it in game, P13/P14 supply data/actions, P25 versions layouts and P27 packages localizations.
screens.backend: Runtime UI tree, DPI-scale layout engine, input/focus routing, style renderer, binding validation and localization support.
screens.acceptance: A menu adapts to 16:9 and ultrawide previews without clipped text, and button navigation works on keyboard/controller.
screens.ai: Generate editable HUD/menu layouts using theme tokens; validate focus, safe areas and localization.
screens.verificationScenario: Author responsive HUD/menu widget.

screens.title: Playtest Studio
screens.placement: Playtest workspace; also F5 from World
screens.purpose: Run the actual game in an embedded or standalone session with safe tools for debugging and repeating gameplay situations.
screens.surface: Dominant live game viewport with optional gamepad overlays, pause/stop/possess controls, FPS/perf HUD and session identifiers.
screens.panels: Session browser, runtime entity tree, variable watches, test presets, logs, recordings, bookmarks, input diagnostics, stats.
screens.actions: Start/stop/restart/eject, possess actor, spawn controlled test entities, set time/weather, bookmark frame, record inputs and replay.
screens.data: PlaytestSession, RuntimeSnapshot, InputTrace, DebugCommand, Bookmark, CrashArtifact and PerfCapture.
screens.connections: Uses P02 scenes, P13 code, P14 graph, P15 NPC AI, P17 UI tests and P16 network simulation; feeds P22 and P23.
screens.backend: Separate runtime context/process where feasible, entity/asset hot reload rules, debugger bridge, input capture and reliable cleanup.
screens.acceptance: Launching and stopping repeatedly does not corrupt the editing scene; a packaged player matches essential gameplay behavior.
screens.ai: Guide or automate limited gameplay routes; capture controller inputs, replay traces and defects.
screens.verificationScenario: Run a saved playtest route.

screens.title: Testing & QA Studio
screens.placement: Analyze > Testing; UI Testing tab is P17
screens.purpose: Organize deterministic automated and manual quality checks for the editor, runtime, assets, accessibility and platform release.
screens.surface: Results dashboard with suite counts, failures, trends, search/filter and selected-test evidence.
screens.panels: Test explorer, execution configs, coverage, logs, crash cases, defect tracker, CI status, reports and regression history.
screens.actions: Define suite, run selected tests, rerun failure, compare builds, attach reproduction, mark severity and export report.
screens.data: TestSuite, TestCase, TestRun, Assertion, Evidence, BugReport, CrashReport and CIJob.
screens.connections: Invokes P17 UI checks, P21 playtests, P16 network tests and P18 build gates; shares failure traces with P39 Console.
screens.backend: Test orchestration, Catch2/CTest bridge, game automation hooks, report aggregation, test evidence storage, crash symbols.
screens.acceptance: A deliberately broken gameplay case is reported with exact assertion, log and reproduction; release can be blocked by gate policy.
screens.ai: Generate tests from requirements, triage crashes and deduplicate defects with project-specific evidence.
screens.verificationScenario: Diagnose a known failing regression.

screens.title: Performance Profiler
screens.placement: Analyze > Profiler; dockable capture view
screens.purpose: Reveal CPU, GPU, memory, asset streaming and frame-time bottlenecks without resorting to speculative visual judgments.
screens.surface: Frame-time timeline with CPU/GPU lanes, profiler tree and capture timeline; optional synchronized game screenshot.
screens.panels: Capture sessions, call tree, render passes, memory allocation chart, shader hot spots, streaming IO, regressions and budgets.
screens.actions: Start capture, pause, select frame, search cost centers, compare baselines, set frame budget, export capture and link offender.
screens.data: ProfilerCapture, MetricSample, FrameMarker, CallTree, GPUEvent, MemoryAllocationEvent and RegressionBaseline.
screens.connections: P02/P21/P18 provide sessions; P31 render settings and P30 terrain streaming respond to findings; P22 enforces budgets.
screens.backend: Tracy instrumentation, GPU timestamp queries, memory labels, render graph instrumentation, capture file format and comparators.
screens.acceptance: A sample bottleneck can be traced from frame spike to a named render pass or function with repeatable metrics on defined hardware.
screens.ai: Explain frame traces and rank optimization candidates; accept only measured improvements.
screens.verificationScenario: Find slow GPU/CPU pass and compare traces.

screens.title: Asset Hub / Content Browser
screens.placement: Content rail / bottom dock; full view on demand
screens.purpose: Provide authoritative search, import, dependency and lifecycle tools for every asset in a WorldForge project.
screens.surface: Resizable tree/grid/list browser with thumbnails, type filters, metadata, dependency graph, previews and import tasks.
screens.panels: Favorites/collections, project folders, tags, import status, referencers, unused asset report, source provenance and asset health.
screens.actions: Import, rename, move, duplicate, reimport, find references, replace reference, validate, bulk tag, migrate and reveal file.
screens.data: AssetRegistry, AssetID, source URI, content hash, dependency edges, import settings, cooked cache and provenance metadata.
screens.connections: Every authoring page creates/consumes assets through P24; P36 import workflow writes registry; P25 versions source files.
screens.backend: Filesystem watcher, local asset-index service/SQLite, dependency graph, thumbnail generator, importer jobs, atomic moves.
screens.acceptance: Renaming or moving an asset preserves references; changing its source triggers only necessary rebuilds and marks invalid dependents.
screens.ai: Hybrid RAG/semantic and exact-ID asset search; deduplication and provenance warnings.
screens.verificationScenario: Locate asset by exact name and visual similarity.

screens.title: Version Control
screens.placement: Source Control icon; history/diff dock
screens.purpose: Expose project revision history, working-tree changes and safe collaborative branches in editor terms.
screens.surface: Changes list, diff/preview, commit editor, branch graph, conflict details and submit history with binary asset indicators.
screens.panels: Git status, staging, commit, fetch/push/pull, branch switch, file-lock and large-asset state, review comments.
screens.actions: Stage, commit, inspect diff, stash changes, resolve text conflict, inspect file history, open affected asset; request locks later.
screens.data: RepositoryState, RevisionID, FileChange, AssetGUID mapping, ConflictRecord and optional lock metadata.
screens.connections: Cross-links to P24 assets, P02 scenes, P26 reviews/tasks and P18 release source revision.
screens.backend: Git CLI/libgit2 evaluation, Git LFS, project conflict adapters and source-control credentials in OS credential store.
screens.acceptance: A user can commit a scene change, reopen earlier version and resolve an edited metadata file without corrupting unrelated assets.
screens.ai: Summarize diffs and potential conflicts; no autonomous merge/deletion without scoped approval.
screens.verificationScenario: Review and revert a scene change.

screens.title: Team & Collaboration
screens.placement: Team icon; dockable project/issue view
screens.purpose: Coordinate task ownership, reviews, asset approvals and permission-based teamwork, without requiring realtime editing on day one.
screens.surface: Project overview with people, tasks/kanban, scene/asset reviews, comments, release milestone calendar and activity.
screens.panels: Members/roles, assignments, review queue, notifications, asset owners, project activity and synchronized repository status.
screens.actions: Create task, assign owner, request review, comment on asset revision, link defect, approve change and track milestone.
screens.data: TeamMember, Role, WorkItem, Review, Comment, Milestone and RevisionLink.
screens.connections: Links bugs P22, source changes P25, assets P24 and release gates P27; online features remain optional.
screens.backend: Future collaboration service, access control, audit log, offline queue/merge and secure project permissions.
screens.acceptance: A reviewer can inspect the exact revision attached to a task and approve/reject it; offline projects remain usable.
screens.ai: Turn milestones into tasks and identify dependency risks; honor project/team authorization.
screens.verificationScenario: Assign and review tasks with permissions.

screens.title: Publishing Studio
screens.placement: Build > Publish; post-artifact release workspace
screens.purpose: Turn verified build artifacts into release candidates with human approvals and destination-specific compliance checks.
screens.surface: Release checklist, store destination cards, metadata/cover art, build artifact selection, validation results and submission status.
screens.panels: Version/changelog, platform package requirements, screenshots/trailers, dependency/license audits, signing and rollback plans.
screens.actions: Select successful build, fill metadata, run validations, create release bundle, upload through authorized integration and stage rollout.
screens.data: ReleaseCandidate, BuildArtifactRef, DestinationProfile, StoreMetadata, ValidationGate, SubmissionRecord.
screens.connections: Consumes P18 successful builds, P22 QA reports, P23 performance budgets and P12 cinematic exports; revisions from P25.
screens.backend: Release orchestrator, platform adapters, secure credentials, metadata validators, checksums, signing, external store APIs later.
screens.acceptance: A release cannot be marked ready when required test, license or signing checks fail; publishing actions require explicit confirmation.
screens.ai: Review release compliance, descriptions, missing licenses and checks; never auto-publish without authorization.
screens.verificationScenario: Prepare a store release candidate.

screens.title: Shader Editor
screens.placement: Materials > Advanced Shader or graph asset
screens.purpose: Expose lower-level shader graphs and source editing with compile diagnostics, hardware resource checks and preview.
screens.surface: Split node/source editing canvas and preview, with syntax-aware inspector and shader permutation/variant metrics.
screens.panels: Shader file tree, function library, code compiler output, reflection uniforms, graph pin types, performance costs.
screens.actions: Edit graph/source, validate types, compile SPIR-V, preview PBR result, change variants, link shader to material and debug errors.
screens.data: ShaderSource, ShaderGraph, SPIRVModule, ShaderReflection, PipelineVariant and CompileDiagnostic.
screens.connections: P06 Material is the consumer; P31 renderer settings affect variants; P23 profiles shaders; P10 VFX consumes GPU shaders.
screens.backend: glslang/shaderc or vetted compiler, SPIR-V validation/optimization, hot-reload staging, shader cache and pipeline reflection.
screens.acceptance: A shader can be edited and recompiled; if compilation fails, the previous valid shader remains active and errors point to nodes/lines.
screens.ai: Suggest graph changes and shaders with compile tests and performance estimates.
screens.verificationScenario: Edit material graph and verify shader compile.

screens.title: Lighting Studio
screens.placement: World > Lighting mode; separate asset tabs
screens.purpose: Set believable lighting and environment conditions with understandable trade-offs between quality and frame cost.
screens.surface: World viewport with light gizmos, exposure histogram, probes, shadow/volume overlays and before/after comparison.
screens.panels: Light list, sun/sky, HDRI, reflection probes, exposure, shadow cascades, atmosphere, fog, baked/real-time GI settings.
screens.actions: Create lights/probes, position light rigs, tune color/intensity, adjust exposure/volumetrics, preview GI and capture reference frame.
screens.data: LightComponent, EnvironmentAsset, LightProbe, ExposureProfile, ShadowConfig, GISettings.
screens.connections: P02 live scene, P06 material preview, P12 cinematics and P31 renderer/scalability modes share lighting data.
screens.backend: Lighting and shadow passes, tone mapping, HDR pipeline, probe baking/import, dynamic GI research for later renderer releases.
screens.acceptance: Light changes affect the same world used by Playtest; an unsupported GI mode gives capability guidance instead of a fake result.
screens.ai: Suggest lighting setups and quality/performance presets with side-by-side measured comparisons.
screens.verificationScenario: Add volumetric lighting without frame spikes.

screens.title: Terrain & Procedural Worlds
screens.placement: World > Terrain/Foliage mode
screens.purpose: Author large landscapes, biomes, roads, foliage and procedural distributions with scalable streaming and clear memory budgets.
screens.surface: Terrain viewport with paint/sculpt brushes, chunk grid, height/slope masks, biome preview and world-partition bounds.
screens.panels: Terrain layers, sculpt/erosion, procedural rules, roads/rivers, scatter graph, foliage types, chunk/streaming stats.
screens.actions: Sculpt heightfield, paint layers, scatter vegetation, bake masks, generate roads, stream tiles and inspect LOD.
screens.data: TerrainAsset, Heightfield, LayerWeightmap, BiomeGraph, InstanceCluster, WorldTile and StreamConfig.
screens.connections: P02 scene contains terrain; P05 produces splat materials; P29 lighting and P35 nav mesh process world tiles; P23 profiles.
screens.backend: Terrain meshing, virtual texturing later, instance rendering, world streaming, data layer systems and cook pipeline.
screens.acceptance: Terrain edits survive reload; only affected tiles rebuild; playable camera transitions between tiles without unacceptable hitching.
screens.ai: Draft biome, road and spline systems constrained by terrain and streaming dependencies.
screens.verificationScenario: Generate terrain road and foliage layers.

screens.title: Render Settings / Graphics Quality
screens.placement: World > Rendering/Project Settings, not always its own tab
screens.purpose: Expose renderer capabilities, quality budgets and platform fallbacks without expecting every developer to understand GPU internals.
screens.surface: Scalability profile editor with a scene preview, capability matrix, GPU feature warnings, quality-performance comparison.
screens.panels: API/backend selection, display resolution, dynamic resolution, anti-aliasing, shadows, GI/reflections, post effects, texture budgets.
screens.actions: Set quality tier, configure renderer flags, compare output, generate shader variants, apply default to project or platform.
screens.data: GraphicsProfile, RenderFeatureSet, ShaderPermutationPolicy, QualityPreset and HardwareCapabilityReport.
screens.connections: P29 Lighting, P28 Shader, P23 Profiler and P18 platform builds consume these settings; P38 stores project defaults.
screens.backend: RHI feature negotiation, renderer configuration, shader/pipeline variant cache and target compatibility validation.
screens.acceptance: Unsupported features are disabled with explanation; quality presets result in real measurable changes in frame cost and visual output.
screens.ai: Recommend measured quality-tier settings, unsupported-feature fallback and capability tests.
screens.verificationScenario: Save portable graphics quality profile.

screens.title: Forge AI Creation Assistant
screens.placement: Global AI utility pane; full plan/review editor on demand
screens.purpose: Help creators edit scenes, code, materials, rigs and test cases using real project context and explicitly approved operations.
screens.surface: Task conversation plus project/asset context picker, structured change plan, affected assets, diff preview, risks and approvals.
screens.panels: Assistant catalog, plan editor, permission scope, suggested tools, preview, tests, audit log, model/usage configuration.
screens.actions: Describe goal, scope selected assets, review proposed commands, edit plan, approve, apply, validate, undo and compare.
screens.data: AIPrompt, ContextSnapshot, ToolSchema, ProposedCommandBatch, Diff, Approval, AuditEntry and CostBudget.
screens.connections: Every editor has exposed safe command APIs; P22 verifies outcomes; P39 logs execution; P24 tracks generated asset provenance.
screens.backend: Model-provider adapter, constrained tools, structured JSON schema, command sandbox, validation/evaluation suite and opt-in networking.
screens.acceptance: A request to place three lights proposes exactly identified objects, shows a diff, applies only after approval and supports rollback.
screens.ai: Forge Director planning, RAG context citations, tool approval, cost/permissions, audit and rollback.
screens.verificationScenario: Approve AI proposal and successfully roll back.

screens.title: Spatial Audio / 360 Sound
screens.placement: Audio > Spatial mode (not separate permanent page)
screens.purpose: Position and debug game sound in 3D space, from positional emitters to binaural rendering and ambisonic environments later.
screens.surface: 3D world preview with emitters, listener/head orientation, attenuation spheres, occlusion rays, room zones and live meters.
screens.panels: Emitter list, HRTF/binaural profile, channel/output layout, distance falloff, Doppler, reverb zones, obstruction and acoustic rays.
screens.actions: Place emitter, edit falloff/cones, listen from virtual player, toggle occlusion, assign room impulse and test headphones.
screens.data: SpatialAudioEmitter, Listener, AttenuationCurve, AcousticZone, ReverbSend, AmbisonicAsset and OutputProfile.
screens.connections: P11 Audio supplies cues and buses; P02/world supplies geometry; P19 collision is optional occlusion source; P21 playtest listens.
screens.backend: Audio spatializer, channel panning, HRTF/DSP integration, acoustic tracing/occlusion and real-time mixer performance budgets.
screens.acceptance: A moving listener produces predictable positional changes; unsupported output formats fall back safely and report capabilities.
screens.ai: Propose spatial placement, HRTF/occlusion/reverb zones with audible/technical validation.
screens.verificationScenario: Configure sound occlusion in rooms.

screens.title: Simulation Studio (fluids, cloth, destruction)
screens.placement: Effects/Simulation > Advanced Simulation modes
screens.purpose: Give artists controlled simulation and baking workflows without conflating fluid/fire/hair solvers with basic rigid-body collision.
screens.surface: Domain-specific scene viewport with solver states, caches, playback time, constraints and collision visualization.
screens.panels: Simulation domains, emitters, solvers, cache paths, bake queue, cloth/hair, volumetric smoke/fire and fracture controls.
screens.actions: Create fluid domain, configure cloth, set collision, run/bake cache, scrub, invalidate affected frames and export optimized runtime form.
screens.data: SimulationGraph, SolverSettings, SimulationCache, BakeTask, DomainBounds, CollisionInputs and SourceAssetRefs.
screens.connections: P19 supplies rigid bodies, P10 VFX consumes baked effects, P12 cinematics previews simulations, P18 cooks runtime derivatives.
screens.backend: Individual solver integrations/research, deterministic caching, frame asset storage, GPU compute jobs and cancellation/recovery.
screens.acceptance: Baking is resumable and reports memory/time; changing a source invalidates only dependent cache and never corrupts authoring data.
screens.ai: Assist simulations and caches with reproducible seeds, safety constraints and compute budgets.
screens.verificationScenario: Cache cloth/particle simulation with deterministic settings.

screens.title: Navigation & NPC World Tools
screens.placement: World > Navigation or Gameplay > NPC AI
screens.purpose: Author pathfinding geometry, navigation zones and traversable links across the real scene.
screens.surface: Scene viewport with navmesh polygons, agent paths, obstacle volumes, heat maps and crowd visualizations.
screens.panels: Nav source list, bake settings, agent profiles, off-mesh links, obstacles, query debugger and world-tile cache.
screens.actions: Mark navigation geometry, bake/update mesh, define traversal costs, create links, query paths and visualize NPC state.
screens.data: NavMeshAsset, AgentProfile, NavArea, OffMeshLink, NavBakeJob, PathQuery and NavTile.
screens.connections: World P02/P30 terrain is input; P15 NPC behavior queries paths; P21 debug and P22 test patrol/crowd scenarios.
screens.backend: Navigation mesh generator/pathfinding runtime, tile cache, deterministic query debug and crowd update budget.
screens.acceptance: A route updates after moving an obstacle or geometry; impossible destinations report failure rather than infinite agent loops.
screens.ai: Suggest navmesh/crowd tuning and inspect path failures with real simulation logs.
screens.verificationScenario: Fix a broken navigation route.

screens.title: Import & Export Pipeline
screens.placement: File > Import; Asset Hub > Import/Export; task dock
screens.purpose: Convert external content into validated WorldForge assets while preserving editability, source provenance and error feedback.
screens.surface: Import wizard with source files, detected types, per-asset preview, options, dependency list, validation and queue progress.
screens.panels: Batch imports, glTF/GLB, images, WAV/OGG/other audio, unit conversion, coordinate orientation, licenses, export presets.
screens.actions: Drag source, configure scale/axes/compression/LOD, preview, validate, import, reimport and export supported interchange assets.
screens.data: ImportJob, SourceAsset, ImportRecipe, ValidationResult, CookedDerivative, SourceLicense and FileHash.
screens.connections: P24 records imported assets; P03/P07/P09 receive content; P18 cooks; P25 stores source files/recipes.
screens.backend: fastgltf, image/audio decoders, guarded file parsers, conversion jobs, async worker queue and progress/error reporting.
screens.acceptance: A valid Blender GLB imports with mesh/material hierarchy; bad paths or malformed source files fail safely with precise errors.
screens.ai: Choose importer settings, report broken resources, propose conversions and verify source-to-cooked fidelity.
screens.verificationScenario: Reimport a modified GLB and update consumers.

screens.title: Plugin & Tools Manager
screens.placement: Tools > Plugins; plugin details as document tabs
screens.purpose: Let third parties extend editor panels, importers, components, build steps and asset tools with permissions and compatibility rules.
screens.surface: Plugin catalog/list, compatibility matrix, details/permissions, installed/enabled state, error and dependency inspection.
screens.panels: Plugin SDK docs, module manifests, extension points, signing/trust, sandbox capabilities, update rollback and diagnostics.
screens.actions: Install approved package, inspect permissions, enable/disable, update, revert, report issue and open developer documentation.
screens.data: PluginManifest, ExtensionPoint, CapabilityPermission, CompatibilityTarget, Signature and InstallRecord.
screens.connections: Extends editors P02-P36, contributes custom commands to P32 AI only after approval, and participates in P18 build packaging.
screens.backend: Versioned C ABI or stable plugin boundary, loader, subprocess sandbox where feasible, signed package checks, crash isolation.
screens.acceptance: A faulty plugin does not corrupt a project or prevent safe-mode startup; incompatible versions are blocked with explanation.
screens.ai: Explain plugin permissions and compatibility; prohibit unreviewed installer or code execution.
screens.verificationScenario: Install a signed compatible extension under review.

screens.title: Project & Engine Settings
screens.placement: Project menu / Settings icon; category dialog
screens.purpose: Provide predictable configuration of project/runtime defaults, input, files, rendering, platforms, privacy and developer preferences.
screens.surface: Searchable settings navigator with per-category pages, modified-state markers, reset and validation hints.
screens.panels: Project identity, startup scene, input maps, frame target, physics timestep, graphics tier, asset paths, editor theme, plugins.
screens.actions: Change settings, compare against defaults, validate unsupported flags, save profile, restore defaults and export configuration.
screens.data: ProjectSettings, UserPreferences, InputActions, PlatformProfile, PrivacyConsent and SettingsSchemaVersion.
screens.connections: Feeds all workspaces; P31 owns detailed rendering configuration; P18 consumes target settings; P40 seeds defaults.
screens.backend: Versioned config schema, secure preference storage, constraints validator, configuration migration and platform capability checks.
screens.acceptance: Settings persist after restart and invalid values are rejected or migrated without silent data loss; editor-only settings stay local.
screens.ai: Explain settings impact and recommend safe profiles; never override permissions or platform gates.
screens.verificationScenario: Change render target settings safely.

screens.title: Console & Diagnostics
screens.placement: Bottom dock, command palette or Window > Console
screens.purpose: Provide unified structured error reporting and safe diagnostics for engine, renderer, scripts, imports, AI, tests and builds.
screens.surface: Compact bottom-dock log with filter levels, search, timestamps, tags and source links; can expand into a large diagnostics view.
screens.panels: Output, warnings, errors, tasks, shader compile, asset import, runtime traces, build logs, crash records and reproduction links.
screens.actions: Filter/search/copy/export logs, open source location, suppress known issue temporarily, attach report and clear local buffer.
screens.data: LogEvent, ErrorCode, Severity, SourceLocation, TaskID, SessionID, DiagnosticBundle and TraceID.
screens.connections: Receives events from all modules; selecting an error opens the correct code P13, shader P28, build P18 or asset P24.
screens.backend: Structured logger, bounded queues, redaction of secrets, crash dump upload opt-in, correlation IDs and portable symbols.
screens.acceptance: A failed shader compile produces one searchable error linked to its originating shader; log collection never leaks credentials.
screens.ai: Classify logs/diagnostics and suggest reproduction steps with links to relevant assets and code.
screens.verificationScenario: Resolve asset/import runtime error from log.

screens.title: Project Creation Wizard
screens.placement: File > New Project from P01; modal wizard
screens.purpose: Create a valid, reproducible project from a small set of templates without requiring knowledge of engine internals.
screens.surface: Step-by-step dialog with template preview, project name/path, supported platform, renderer preset, sample content and summary.
screens.panels: Blank 3D, third-person starter, small simulation sample, future 2D/VR templates; toolchain validation and disk requirements.
screens.actions: Choose template, select path/name, set startup scene and quality preset, validate writable location, create and open project.
screens.data: TemplateManifest, ProjectManifest, ToolchainRequirement, SceneBootstrap, ProjectSettings and CreationReport.
screens.connections: Invoked from P01; results open P02 and initialize P24 asset registry, P25 Git option and P38 settings.
screens.backend: Template expansion, file atomicity, path security, project migration detection, source-control initialization and rollback on error.
screens.acceptance: A Blank 3D project is created with stable IDs and sample scene, then opens with no missing dependencies; failure leaves no half-project.
screens.ai: Recommend templates based on project goals and hardware; preview generated project requirements.
screens.verificationScenario: Create a project from a template and reopen it.
